question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Xi Jinping’s entrenched position as general secretary and president, reinforced by the abolition of term limits and the absence of any designated successor or visible elite opposition, underpins the 95.5% trader consensus that he will remain in office through 2026. Ongoing purges of senior military and party figures, including recent removals from the Central Military Commission, have eliminated potential rivals while signaling continued loyalty requirements ahead of the 21st Party Congress scheduled for late 2027. Analysts note that preparations for that congress center on generational turnover among other leaders rather than Xi’s departure, consistent with his pattern of extending rule into a fourth term. While low-probability events such as a sudden health crisis or unforeseen elite fracture could still alter the outcome before year-end, no recent diplomatic, economic, or internal developments have shifted the prevailing assessment of his dominance.
